newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end higher as Hanbo shock fades.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end higher as Hanbo shock fades.

text.p: Shares rebounded in late trading to end slightly higher on Friday after recouping large losses earlier caused by news that Hanbo Steel Corp had defaulted on debt payments, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed at a provisional 679.56, up 2.65 points. Brokers said bargain hunting and hopes that the Hanbo crisis would be resolved soon fuelled late buying.
"Hanbo's default was the focus of the day, and I thought the market would be more undermined, but bargain hunting lifted individual shares at the end," said Lee Duck-jae of Dongwon Securities.

Hanbo on Thursday failed to honour payments for notes totalling more than five billion won, creditors said. The group chairman said the steelmaker would file for court receivership on Friday. Hanbo has debt totalling 5.7 trillion won.
The index plunged nearly 2.8 percent to a low of 658.18 shortly after the market opened but recovered gruadually to move into positive territory.
Advancers outpaced decliners by 431 to 360, while 110 remained unchanged. Volume was 35.44 million shares.
KEPCO ended at 28,000 won, up 800, on foreign buying. Hyundai Motor rose 1,500 to 24,000 and LG Elec 400 to 11,100.
But banking stocks remained in the blues. Korea First Bank, one of Hanbo's major creditors, fell 360 won to its limit of 4,220. SEOULBANK lost 220 won 4,380.
To avoid a liquidity crunch after Hanbo's default, the Bank of Korea, the central bank, said it would supply one trillion won to commercial banks on Friday through repurchase agreements.
The exchange halted trading in Hanbo and its affiliate Sang-A Pharmaceutical indefinitely.
